title: Single Quotes Make a String Too

learning.python:
In Hello World you wrote a string between double quotes: "Hello World!". Python lets you write a string between single quotes as well:

print('Good morning.')   # prints: Good morning.

Both ways make the same string: 'Good morning.' and "Good morning." are equal. The quotes mark where the string starts and ends, and aren't part of it.

A string ends with the same kind of quote it starts with. One that starts with ' goes on until the next '.

See An Informal Introduction to Python in the Python documentation.
